results.name: first_example_digit_lift
results.description: Among multi-example sets without a shared final digit, yes-rate on non-example targets sharing the FIRST example's final digit (but not the last's) minus yes-rate on targets sharing no example's final digit; the model gives only the last example a lingering digit, so observed above null means a primacy digit effect the model misses.
results.code:
# name: first_example_digit_lift
# description: Among multi-example sets without a shared final digit, yes-rate on non-example targets sharing the FIRST example's final digit (but not the last's) minus yes-rate on targets sharing no example's final digit; the model gives only the last example a lingering digit, so observed above null means a primacy digit effect the model misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    inset = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    D = np.mod(E, 10)
    dmin = np.nanmin(D, axis=1); dmax = np.nanmax(D, axis=1)
    ok = (n >= 2) & (dmin != dmax) & (~inset)
    td = t % 10
    first = D[:, 0]
    last = D[np.arange(len(t)), n - 1]
    anyd = np.any(D == td[:, None], axis=1)
    a = ok & (td == first) & (td != last)
    b = ok & (~anyd)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_set_breadth_dispersion
results.description: Standard deviation across single-example sets (with >=20 responses) of the set-level yes-rate on non-example targets; observed above null means people's generalization breadth varies more from seed to seed (some single numbers suggest broad, others narrow concepts) than the model produces, below means the model makes seeds too different.
results.code:
# name: single_set_breadth_dispersion
# description: Standard deviation across single-example sets (with >=20 responses) of the set-level yes-rate on non-example targets; observed above null means people's generalization breadth varies more from seed to seed (some single numbers suggest broad, others narrow concepts) than the model produces, below means the model makes seeds too different.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    isex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    ok = (n == 1) & ~isex
    s = pd.DataFrame({"s": df["number_set"].astype(str).to_numpy()[ok], "r": r[ok]})
    g = s.groupby("s")["r"].agg(["mean", "size"])
    g = g[g["size"] >= 20]
    if len(g) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return float(g["mean"].std())

results.name: single_example_yes_gap
results.description: Yes-rate on single-example sets minus yes-rate on multi-example sets (non-example targets only); observed above null means the model under-generalizes from one example (too narrow/conservative on n=1), below means it over-generalizes.
results.code:
# name: single_example_yes_gap
# description: Yes-rate on single-example sets minus yes-rate on multi-example sets (non-example targets only); observed above null means the model under-generalizes from one example (too narrow/conservative on n=1), below means it over-generalizes.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    inset = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    a = (n == 1) & (~inset)
    b = (n > 1) & (~inset)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_proximity_gap
results.description: In single-example sets, yes-rate on targets within 15 of the example minus yes-rate on targets more than 40 away; the incumbent now has a graded (symmetric-width) magnitude band, so observed above null means people still generalize from one example by magnitude similarity more steeply than the band produces, below means less.
results.code:
# name: single_example_proximity_gap
# description: In single-example sets, yes-rate on targets within 15 of the example minus yes-rate on targets more than 40 away; the incumbent now has a graded (symmetric-width) magnitude band, so observed above null means people still generalize from one example by magnitude similarity more steeply than the band produces, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    dist = np.abs(E[:, 0] - t)
    ok = (n == 1) & (dist > 0)
    a = ok & (dist <= 15)
    b = ok & (dist > 40)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: multi_set_size_yes_slope
results.description: Among multi-example sets, yes-rate on non-example targets for 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; the model has no explicit size principle (only property sharing), so observed below null means people narrow generalization with more examples more than modelled, above means they narrow less (or broaden).
results.code:
# name: multi_set_size_yes_slope
# description: Among multi-example sets, yes-rate on non-example targets for 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; the model has no explicit size principle (only property sharing), so observed below null means people narrow generalization with more examples more than modelled, above means they narrow less (or broaden).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    isex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    a = ~isex & (n == 4); b = ~isex & (n == 2)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: round_number_target_lift
results.description: Among non-example targets for sets whose examples are NOT all multiples of 10, yes-rate on targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes-rate on other targets; the model credits multiples of 10 only when all examples share it, so observed above null means a round-number endorsement bias the model misses, below means people shun round targets.
results.code:
# name: round_number_target_lift
# description: Among non-example targets for sets whose examples are NOT all multiples of 10, yes-rate on targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes-rate on other targets; the model credits multiples of 10 only when all examples share it, so observed above null means a round-number endorsement bias the model misses, below means people shun round targets.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    isex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    allten = np.all(np.isnan(E) | (np.mod(E, 10) == 0), axis=1)
    ok = ~isex & ~allten
    rnd = np.mod(t, 10) == 0
    a = ok & rnd; b = ok & ~rnd
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: inrange_nearest_example_gap
results.description: Multi-example sets, non-example targets strictly inside [min,max]: yes-rate for targets within 5 of the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets more than 15 from every example; the model gives all in-range targets full magnitude credit, so observed above null means people use proximity to individual examples (exemplar similarity) that the model misses, below means they avoid near neighbours.
results.code:
# name: inrange_nearest_example_gap
# description: Multi-example sets, non-example targets strictly inside [min,max]: yes-rate for targets within 5 of the nearest example minus yes-rate for targets more than 15 from every example; the model gives all in-range targets full magnitude credit, so observed above null means people use proximity to individual examples (exemplar similarity) that the model misses, below means they avoid near neighbours.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    isex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(E, axis=1)
    d = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    ok = (n >= 2) & ~isex & (t > lo) & (t < hi)
    a = ok & (d <= 5); b = ok & (d > 15)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: single_example_up_down_asymmetry
results.description: Single-example sets, targets within 30 of the example: yes-rate on targets above the example minus yes-rate on targets below it; the model's band uses one width for both directions, so observed above null means people extend a single example upward more readily than the model (beyond seed multiples), below means downward.
results.code:
# name: single_example_up_down_asymmetry
# description: Single-example sets, targets within 30 of the example: yes-rate on targets above the example minus yes-rate on targets below it; the model's band uses one width for both directions, so observed above null means people extend a single example upward more readily than the model (beyond seed multiples), below means downward.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    isex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    e = E[:, 0]
    ok = (n == 1) & ~isex & (np.abs(t - e) <= 30)
    a = ok & (t > e); b = ok & (t < e)
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
